## Summary
<sup>What this changes and why. No need to recap CI-verifiable facts (test counts, build status) — CI reports those itself.</sup>

## Behavior changes
<sup>List every user-visible behavior that differs after this PR. "None" is a claim reviewers will check. Refactors that change any observable behavior must declare it here.</sup>

## Hot paths
<sup>Does this add I/O, network calls, or blocking work to a critical path (OCR trigger, translation cascade, overlay render, continuous-mode tick)? Which, and why is that acceptable?</sup>

## Testing evidence
<sup>Environment used, the flow you exercised, and what you observed. Screenshots welcome where UI is involved.</sup>

## Spec sync
<sup>Specs must reflect what was actually built — keep them aligned on every merge.</sup>

- [ ] `features.md` — AC checkboxes updated to reflect current implementation state
- [ ] If an architectural decision was made during implementation: ADR created or updated in `specs/architecture/adr/`
- [ ] If ADR created: `specs/architecture/architecture.md` updated accordingly
- [ ] No behavior shipped that isn't declared in the User Story or AC of the originating Issue

## AI assistance
<sup>What role did AI play, and to what extent? (e.g. "written primarily by Claude Code", "consulted for design, authored manually", "none"). Attribution: "Autogenerated with AI" — never Co-Authored-By: Claude.</sup>

## Checklist
<sup>Please check all that apply.</sup>

- [ ] `dotnet build --configuration Release` — zero errors, zero new warnings
- [ ] `dotnet test` — all tests pass including `Category=Architecture`
- [ ] `dotnet csharpier --check .` — no formatting drift
- [ ] No secrets, credentials, or hardcoded connection strings in staged files (`secret-scan` hook cleared)
- [ ] Spec sync section above is complete
- [ ] I have personally reviewed and understand the code being submitted
